definitions: To start a new hobby, sport, or activity.
To accept an offer or a challenge.
To begin to deal with or discuss something.
To lift something from the ground or a surface.
To shorten a piece of clothing.
examples: She decided to take up painting in her retirement.
This sofa takes up too much room in the living room.
He took up the offer of a job in London.
The committee will take up the matter at their next meeting.
He took up the book from the table.
My trousers are too long; I need to take them up.
